title: Макс становится су-шефом и пропажа Насти  (Max Becomes Sous-Chef and Nastya Disappears)

segments.t: After Senya and Fedya refuse to cover for Lyova without extra pay, Chef Barinov shocks the kitchen by appointing Max as acting sous-chef. Meanwhile, Nastya's mother calls Kostya in a panic because Nastya left for work in the morning and never arrived.
Агузок, хочешь быть су-шефом?
Да вы все равно не назначите.
Я работаю недавно, у меня опыта мало.
Я сказал, не умничай.
Ты уже су-шеф.
Переделаешь суп и приступай.
Да, Настя?
Вот так целый час.
Где Настя?
Я не знаю.
Она с утра к вам поехала.
Нет ее у нас.
Может, она к нему домой вернулась?
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
Агузок, хочешь быть су-шефом?
'Oguzok, do you want to be sous-chef?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'rookie' before landing on 'sous-chef'.
Да вы все равно не назначите.
'Come on, you will not appoint me anyway.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'yes' before landing on 'to set'. Nastya answers right away.
Я работаю недавно, у меня опыта мало.
'I have only worked here a short time, I have very little experience.' The meaning hinges on 'I' working together with 'little' in spoken Russian.
Я сказал, не умничай.
'I told you, do not get smart with me.' Max anchors the line on 'I', while 'to act smart' completes the thought.
Ты уже су-шеф.
'You are already the sous-chef.' Chef Viktor addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'sous-chef'. Nastya answers right away.
Переделаешь суп и приступай.
'Redo the soup and get started.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'to redo' before landing on 'get to'.
Да, Настя?
'Yes, where is Nastya?' Max brings out the contrast between 'yes' and 'Nastya' in a few short words.
Вот так целый час.
'It has been like this for a whole hour.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'there you go' and finishing on 'hour'. Nastya answers right away.
Где Настя?
'Where is Nastya?' In Russian, the idea of 'where' flows naturally into 'Nastya' without extra filler words.
Я не знаю.
'I do not know.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'I' before landing on 'know'.
Она с утра к вам поехала.
'She left for your place first thing this morning.' In Russian, the idea of 'she' flows naturally into 'to go' without extra filler words. Nastya answers right away.
Нет ее у нас.
'She is not here with us.' The meaning hinges on 'there is no' working together with 'us' in spoken Russian.
Может, она к нему домой вернулась?
'Maybe she went back home to his place?' The meaning hinges on 'maybe' working together with 'returned' in spoken Russian. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.
